title: English File Intermediate, File 9: third conditional, quantifiers

fixIt.text: If I had left earlier, I would catch the bus.
fixIt.explain: Third conditional: if + had + past participle, would have + past participle.

fixIt.text: If she had studied, she would have pass.
We wouldn't have met if you hadn't came to the party.
fixIt.explain: hadn't + past participle: come, came, come.

fixIt.text: If I knew about the party, I would have gone.
fixIt.explain: Imagined past: if + had + past participle.

fixIt.text: If it hadn't rained, we would have went to the beach.
fixIt.explain: would have + past participle: go, went, gone.

fixIt.text: I don't have many time to check my messages.
There are too much apps on my phone.
fixIt.explain: apps are countable: too many apps.

fixIt.text: I have a few money left, so I can't buy a new laptop.
fixIt.explain: money is uncountable: a little money.

fixIt.text: Is there enough batteries for the camera?
fixIt.explain: batteries is plural: Are there enough …?

fixIt.text: There isn't some milk in the fridge.

fixIt.explain: How she speaks is an adverb: well.

fixIt.text: Luckily, nobody was hurt. It was a luck escape.
fixIt.explain: Before a noun, an adjective: a lucky escape.

builder.text: If I'd known, I would have come.
builder.tip: if + had + past participle, would have + past participle.
alternatives: I would have come if I'd known.

builder.text: How much time do you have?
There are too many people here.

radio.title: A lucky day
radio.text: Last year I nearly missed my sister's wedding. My bus broke down on the way to Siem Reap, and there wasn't any phone signal. If a kind farmer hadn't stopped, I would have waited for hours. He took me to the next town on his motorbike, and I caught another bus. I arrived just in time. If he hadn't helped me, I wouldn't have seen my sister get married. I have very few photos of that day, but I will never forget it.
